title: Zipper Started as a Name for Boots
hook: The name “zipper” came from a rubber boot brand in 1923
summary: Zipper was originally a name for rubber boots in 1923. The fastener ended up taking the name.

text: You pull zippers up and down several times a day.
But “zipper” wasn’t originally the name of this little device.
In 1893, American inventor Whitcomb Judson patented a device.
He called it the Clasp Locker.
In 1913, Gideon Sundback made it sturdier and began selling it.
This time, the name was “Hookless Fastener.”
In 1923, the American company B.F. Goodrich
attached the fastener to rubber boots.
One quick pull was all it took to close them.

panels.mean: the sound of something moving quickly

text: But people started using the name
for the fastener instead of the boots.

panels.text: So the fastener stole the boots’ name

text: Zippers beat buttons on trouser flies in 1937.
That was when French designers embraced zippers for men’s trousers.
